items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the penal law, in relation to permitting 4-H certified
shooting sports instructors to supervise and instruct persons under sixteen
years of age at shooting ranges
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6401

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the penal law, in relation to permit-
ting 4-H certified shooting sports instructors to supervise and instruct
persons under sixteen years of age at shooting ranges

 
PURPOSE:

To allow 4-H certified shooting sports instructors to supervise and
instruct persons under sixteen years of age at shooting ranges

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 19 of section 265.00 of the penal law to
add "a New York state 4-H certified shooting sports instructor" to the
definition of a "Duly authorized instructor"

Section 2 amends paragraphs 7, 7-c, and 7-d of subdivision a of section
265.20 of the penal law to add "a New York State 4-H certified shooting
sports instructor"

Section 3 adds a definition of a New York state 4-H certified shooting
instructor

Section 4 establishes the effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The 4-H Shooting Sports Instructor training program is specifically
tailored to train adults to instruct young people. 4-H Shooting Sports
offers comprehensive Instructor Certification training, as part of the
National 4-H Shooting Sports Program, that focuses on life skills and
positive youth development within the education and training components
of the core curriculum disciplines, including risk management. The 4-H
Shooting Sports State Instructor Training consists of a nationally
approved curriculum and requires applicants to complete a minimum of 14
hours of education and training per curriculum discipline area, includ-
ing risk management, and pass specific requirements in order to qualify
for Certification. All instructor applicants must also pass a background
check and be approved prior to attending any New York State 4-H Shooting
Sports Instructor Certification Training Course. This bill will allow
4-H Certified Shooting Instructors to legally supervise and instruct
young people, under the age of sixteen, at shooting ranges.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately
